correctness.rationale: For every n≥3 and six consecutive length-three rank patterns, conditioning on prescribed distinct images at positions (t,t+1,t+2) leaves n−3 uniform path components; the number of disjoint cycles has conditional mean Z_closed+H_{n−3}. Complete fixed-cycle length 1,2,3 counts (binomial fixed-point sums, pair reversal possibilities, and exactly two possible 3-cycles) yield the displayed S_p polynomial vector. Subtracting (n−2)(H_n−H_{n−3})/6 gives six rational covariances (3n−2,3n−8,3n−8,4−3n,4−3n,10−3n)/(6n(n−1)), including exceptional sign n=3 for pattern321. The peak orientations 132/231 give difference (n−2)/(n(n−1)) and sum −2/(3n(n−1)); analogous valley. I independently enumerated full uniform S_n for n=3,…,7 and recomputed cycle+rank-pattern covariances as exact fractions for each pattern, all matching. The infinite n claim follows symbolic closed-cycle table formulas, not this bounded enumeration.
residual_risks: No finite check replaces the analytic proof; claims quantified as in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: Cycle count measures a global permutation decomposition, while consecutive triple patterns are natural local statistics. The six-type covariance classification gives a sharp and non-obvious sign pattern (including an n=3 boundary exception), and a cancellation mechanism in which oriented peak/valley contrast is O(1/n) but combined peak count is O(1/n²). This is a motivated dependence invariant beyond textbook marginal enumeration.
residual_risks: Value depends on precisely stated natural object and invariant; no general downstream theorem claimed.

limitations: Uniform permutations and consecutive patterns length 3 only; no higher mixed moments or other lengths.
